entries.definition: wrong in e.g. opinion or judgment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the judgment while leaving the intention unblamed - being led wrong is a softer charge than being wrong.

entries.definition: wrong in e.g. opinion or judgment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Records the error and nothing else, no reproach attaching, where *misguided* still suggests the opinion was badly arrived at.

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and judicial in weight, handing the blame down as a finding rather than an outburst - the cold end of *criminal*.
examples: adultery is as reprehensible for a husband as for a wife

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the fault in the thing itself rather than in the verdict on it, imputing wickedness where *reprehensible* only assigns blame.

entries.definition: contrary to conscience or morality or law
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The family's flat verdict, condemning without heat and reaching conscience, morality and law with the same single word.
examples: it is wrong for the rich to take advantage of the poor

entries.definition: moving at very high speed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The danger sits in the picture rather than in any verdict - a pace fast enough to break a neck, which can sound thrilling as readily as reckless.

entries.definition: of uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare formation, saying only that an outcome is full of chance, without the wariness *chancy* packs into the same idea.

entries.definition: of uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and shrugging - the outcome is handed to luck, which is enough to mark the thing as not worth counting on.

entries.definition: involving or causing danger or risk; liable to hurt or harm
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unarguable - it states that harm can follow and leaves the judging to someone else, where *unsafe* already faults the thing.

entries.definition: (of persons) dangerously reckless or violent as from urgency or despair
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Aimed at a person rather than a situation - past caution and liable to violence, and the despair behind it does nothing to soften the warning.

entries.definition: of uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, with a gambler's wince in it - the odds are being felt rather than merely noted.
examples: an extremely dicey future on a brave new world of liquid nitrogen, tar, and smog

entries.definition: of uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and dismissive - the thing is not just uncertain but not to be relied on, the most distrustful way of putting the same risk.

entries.definition: involving risk or danger
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and classifying - it registers danger as a property to be assessed, cooler than *risky*, which sounds like advice.

entries.definition: intended to entrap
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns outright, because here the danger is designed - something is laying a trap, and the word says so.

entries.definition: biting or given to biting
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and dry for something with teeth - it charges a creature with the habit of biting, not merely a single bite.
examples: they deliberately gave me a skittish and mordacious mount

entries.definition: caught in a difficult or dangerous situation
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal, and the image does the work: the danger is a trap someone is caught in rather than a failing of theirs.
examples: there I was back on the hook

entries.definition: fraught with danger
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Heightened and declamatory - it announces danger with a flourish that *perilous* manages without.
examples: a parlous journey on stormy seas

entries.definition: fraught with danger
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Grave and unironic - danger at full weight, more formal than *dangerous* and with none of the hedging in *chancy*.
examples: a perilous voyage across the Atlantic in a small boat

entries.definition: involving risk or danger
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Everyday and weighing - it frames the danger as something one might knowingly take on, where *hazardous* only labels it.
examples: extremely risky going out in the tide and fog

entries.definition: involving or causing danger or risk; liable to hurt or harm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Measures the thing against a standard of safety it fails, so the danger arrives with a fault attached that *dangerous* leaves off.

entries.definition: involving risk or danger
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Relishes the danger instead of warning against it, giving the same risk a heat that *hazardous* keeps out.

entries.definition: sharply contrasted in character or purpose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Casts the unlikeness as a matched opposition, two things defined against each other rather than merely unalike as in *different*.
examples: practices entirely antithetical to her professed beliefs

entries.definition: sharply contrasted in character or purpose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The fuller and weightier-sounding form beside *antithetic*, carrying the same sense of two things set squarely against each other.
examples: practices entirely antithetical to her professed beliefs

entries.definition: of many different kinds purposefully arranged but lacking any uniformity
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Turns difference into a made mixture — the variety is arranged, though nothing in it matches.

entries.definition: very opposed in nature or character or purpose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Marks unlikeness strong enough to amount to opposition, past the plain difference of *different* but short of the total inversion of *diametric*.
examples: acts contrary to our code of ethics
the facts point to a contrary conclusion

entries.definition: strikingly different; tending to contrast
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Makes the difference visible — the unlikeness is what strikes you when the two are set side by side.

entries.definition: strikingly different; tending to contrast
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Frames that same striking unlikeness as a property a thing has rather than an effect it produces, the more analytic-sounding of the pair with *contrasting*.

entries.definition: characterized by opposite extremes; completely opposed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the two at opposite ends of a single line, so the difference is total rather than merely sharp as in *contrasting*.
examples: in diametric contradiction to his claims

entries.definition: characterized by opposite extremes; completely opposed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The extended form of *diametric*, identical in force and a shade more formal in shape.

entries.definition: unlike in nature or quality or form or degree
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare statement of unlikeness, fixing no degree — it says two things are not the same and stops there.
examples: took different approaches to the problem
on different sides of the issue
this meeting was different from the earlier one

entries.definition: fundamentally different or distinct in quality or kind
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Places the unlikeness at the root — a difference of kind rather than of degree, deeper than the surface difference of *different*.
examples: such disparate attractions as grand opera and game fishing

entries.definition: (often followed by ‘from’) not alike; different in nature or quality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: States the unlikeness as a clean separation of one thing from another, without any of the extremity of *diametric*.
examples: the word ‘nationalism’ is used in at least two distinct senses
a tree related to but quite distinct from the European beech
management had interests quite distinct from those of their employees

entries.definition: (often followed by ‘from’) not alike; different in nature or quality
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the same unlikeness in terms of what can be told apart, so the difference is one that survives inspection, where *distinct* just asserts it.

entries.definition: diverging from another or from a standard
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Makes the difference a moving apart rather than a settled state, and lets a standard be the thing departed from, where *disparate* simply finds two things unlike.

entries.definition: characterized by opposite extremes; completely opposed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest way to state complete opposition, where *diametric* and *polar* dress the same total reversal in a figure.

entries.definition: characterized by opposite extremes; completely opposed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Renders the opposition as two extremes with nothing between them, giving the contrast a fixed maximum that *contrary* leaves open-ended.

entries.definition: of many different kinds purposefully arranged but lacking any uniformity
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Spreads the same idea across the kinds themselves, a plural of difference, where *assorted* keeps attention on the mixing.
examples: his disguises are many and various
various experiments have failed to disprove the theory
cited various reasons for his behavior

entries.definition: sufficiently significant to affect the whole world
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Trades gravity for reach — the effect is felt across the whole world, and the word keeps the physical jolt of its image.

entries.definition: highly significant or important especially bringing about or marking the beginning of a new development or era
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The active twin of *epochal* — it credits the thing with making the new beginning rather than merely marking it.

entries.definition: highly significant or important especially bringing about or marking the beginning of a new development or era
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Adds a boundary to the weight: not just great effect but the opening of something new, which *momentous* never requires.
examples: epochal decisions made by Roosevelt and Churchill

entries.definition: serving as or based on evidence
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries no appraisal at all — it marks only that something rests on or supplies evidence, so it sits outside any scale of weight.
examples: evidential signs of a forced entry

entries.definition: serving as or based on evidence
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The stiffer, more formal twin of *evidential*, and just as free of praise or blame.

entries.definition: far-reaching and thoroughgoing in effect especially on the nature of something
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points downward rather than upward: the effect reaches what a thing is, describing depth of change instead of how much it is admired.
examples: the fundamental revolution in human values that has occurred
committed the fundamental error of confusing spending with extravagance

entries.definition: important in effect or meaning
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: More insistent than *significant* — it claims the thing matters and should be treated accordingly, not merely that it registers.

entries.definition: fairly large or important in effect; influential
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Deliberately unemphatic — it grants real effect and influence while stopping far short of *monumental*.
examples: played a large role in the negotiations

entries.definition: of very great significance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Lifts *significant* to a height where the weight itself is the point, grave and admiring at once.
examples: deciding to drop the atom bomb was a very momentous decision

entries.definition: of outstanding significance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Makes the significance imposing, something that stands over whatever is beside it, where *noteworthy* only asks you to look.

entries.definition: worthy of attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A modest claim: it asks for attention and promises nothing beyond it.
examples: a noteworthy fact is that her students rarely complain
a noteworthy advance in cancer research

entries.definition: far-reaching and thoroughgoing in effect especially on the nature of something
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Where *fundamental* is structural this one is grave, reaching the same way into a thing's nature but spoken with awe.

entries.definition: worthy of attention
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Stronger than *noteworthy* on the same ground — attention is compelled rather than merely deserved, and admiration comes with it.
